turn_text: From the Ag Information Network, this is today's group grower report. While many say President Trump's tariffs set to take effect against Canada and Mexico on Tuesday are merely a negotiating tool. But U.S. representatives Susan DelBenet of Washington's First District says tariffs and trade would be hugely impactful to industries and households in every district across the country.

Trump's plan to impose tariffs on Canada, Mexico, and China with emergency powers will increase costs for American households by over $1,200 per year. And his reciprocal tariff plan will cost households in additional $2,700 to $3,400 per year. Low and middle income earners, including farmers, will be the hardest hit.
And trade wars Delbene says always impact agriculture.

What is being done to protect farmers? Are we not concerned about the massive retaliation against our farmers that a trade war brings? It always impacts agriculture. Are my colleagues, my Republican colleagues in particular, going to allow President Trump to raise taxes on the American people without a say? This,
Del Benet says, is a congressional matter.

The Constitution is very clear about this. Congress, not the president, has the power to impose taxes and tariffs and to regulate foreign commerce. That is one of the basic functions of the Ways and Means Committee.
Tune in tomorrow for more on trade and tariffs from First District Representative, Susan Del Benet.
And this has been today's Frugro Report.
I'm Bob Larson from the Ag Information Network.
